title: Overwritten paragraph for editing
subject: English Language
source: Written for english-language/y10 lesson 9 (Overwritten paragraph for editing (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 9: Language for effect: figurative language and precise vocabulary. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Figurative language with purpose
points: Every image must fit the mood
Extend one image rather than mix five
Check: does the reader see it at once?

head: Not this
This
rows: The extremely dark, gloomy, shadowy, frightening, black night was like a monster like a beast like a void.
The night pressed against the windows like a held breath.

keywords.def: giving human qualities to non-human things
piling up adjectives and images until meaning is lost

questions.q: Upgrade with one precise verb: 'The wind went through the trees making a loud noise.'
questions.a: For example: The wind tore through the trees.

questions.q: Write a personification of a clock in an exam hall.
questions.a: For example: The clock on the wall counted every second out loud, as if it enjoyed it.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, rewrite the overwritten paragraph on the pupil PDF using precise verbs and one extended image. Starter: 'The fog...'
questions.a: A controlled paragraph with precise vocabulary and one sustained image.

questions.q: Extend: label each image and explain its effect in one line.
Stretch: write a sentence where the metaphor carries the mood without any adjectives.
questions.a: For example: The house sulked behind its hedge.

options: The very thick, grey, damp, cold fog was everywhere.
The fog was like a blanket like a wall like a ghost.
questions.a: C) The fog swallowed the street.. One strong verb does the work; the others overwrite.
A) too many adjectives and images

questions.q: Answer the ponder in one sentence.
questions.a: Often yes: a precise verb shows the action and the mood at once.
